dedupe_keys.name: enabling programmable multiband high capacity optical transceivers

description: Laia Nadal and colleagues document this resource in the B5G-OPEN community. The experiment evaluates programmable multiband sliceable bandwidth/bitrate-variable optical transceivers over up to 50.47 km of standard single-mode fibre. Coverage is the physical communication testbed described in the paper. It demonstrates a basis for flexible capacity scaling; the native abstract does not list every band, data rate or measured error statistic. The test is not treated as a carrier deployment, and an independently downloadable waveform dataset or transceiver implementation is not established. Zenodo provides the descriptive publication with open access; its stated licence is cc-by-4.0. Its publication licence does not establish a code licence or source-code availability. A limitation is that the native metadata do not establish all implementation settings, uncertainty bounds or independent reproducibility. Only descriptive metadata were inspected. Related records and companion papers retain their source-defined roles; they do not imply independent measurements. A related registered abstract describes a 60-Gb/s C+S prototype over 25.2 km; this is a distinct configuration within the transceiver test programme, not the same 50.47-km experiment. The test provides an assessment of programmable optical transmission over a physical fibre link.
